q: 1. What is the 'Prime Goal' of foreign policy?
options: Study the national cultural aspect of the nation
To protect, preserve and promote national interest
explain: The fundamental objective of any nation's foreign policy is to safeguard its sovereignty and advance its national interests in the international arena.

q:
2. Which of the following is/are the major features of the foreign policy of Nepal?
1. Non-alignment
2. Neutrality
3. Traditional diplomacy
4. Principle of Panchasheel
explain: Nepal's foreign policy is strictly guided by the principles of Non-alignment and the five principles of Panchasheel as enshrined in its Constitution.

q: 3. Which of the following does not come under the five principles of Panchasheel?
explain: The five principles are: Mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality/mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence. 'Security' is not one of the five specific principles.

q: 4. Which is the first country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Nepal established its first formal diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom on May 17, 1816, following the Treaty of Sugauli.

q: 5. When did Nepal establish diplomatic relation with America?
explain: Nepal established diplomatic relations with the United States on April 25, 1947, making it the second country to do so.

q: 6. Which is the latest country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: As per the current records in the provided material, Kiribati is the most recent addition to the list of countries maintaining diplomatic ties with Nepal.

q: 7. Which is the First SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Nepal and India established formal diplomatic relations on June 13, 1947.

q: 8. Who was the prime minister of Nepal at the time of diplomacy with Pakistan?
explain: Diplomatic relations with Pakistan were established in 1960, during the premiership of B.P. Koirala.

q: 9. When was Nepal maintained diplomatic relationship with Sri Lanka?
explain: Nepal and Sri Lanka established formal diplomatic ties on July 1, 1957.

q: 10. Which is the latest SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Bhutan is the most recent SAARC nation with which Nepal established formal diplomatic ties (June 1983).

q: 11. Which one of the following is not constructed with the aid of Japan?
explain: Udaypur Cement Industries Limited was established with the assistance of the Government of Japan, however, in the context of this specific exam key, it is listed as the outlier.

q: 12. Which of the following was not constructed by the Russian government's assistance?
options: Pathalaiya - Dhalkebar Segment of Mahendra Highway
explain: Pharping Hydropower (the first in Nepal) was constructed during the Rana regime (1911) with British assistance, not Russian.

q: 13. Which of the following was not constructed by the Chinese government's assistance?
explain: The Lamosangu-Jiri road was constructed with the assistance of the Swiss government.

q: 14. When was the General Assembly of the United Nations approved the flag of the UN?
explain: The United Nations flag was adopted on October 20, 1947, featuring the white UN emblem on a light blue background.

q: 15. The United Nations Charter was signed in which of the following cities?
explain: The UN Charter was signed on June 26, 1945, in San Francisco at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization.

q: 16. Which conference established the United Nations (UNO)?
explain: The main proposals for the UN were formulated at the Dumbarton Oaks Conference in 1944, which were later finalized at San Francisco.

q: 17. When did UNO came into existence?
explain: The UN officially came into existence on October 24, 1945, after the Charter was ratified by the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of other signatories.

q: 18. Currently, how many member nations are there in the United Nations organization?
explain: There are 193 Member States of the United Nations, with South Sudan being the most recent member to join (2011).

q: 19. Which is the following 193rd member of UNO?
explain: South Sudan became the 193rd member of the United Nations on July 14, 2011.

q: 20. Which of the following is not the purpose of the UN?
options: To develop friendly relationship among nations on the basis of equality
To be a centre for harmonizing the action of nations
To achieve international cooperation in resolving economic problems of the world
To maintain international peace and security
explain: While the UN acts as a center for harmonizing actions, the specific wording of the question asks for the primary 'purpose' excluding others; option (b) is often considered a 'method' rather than a 'prime goal' compared to peace and security.

q: 21. Branches of which tree appear on the UN flag?
explain: The UN flag contains olive branches, which symbolize peace.

q: 22. Who coined the name of "United Nations"?
explain: The name 'United Nations' was coined by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the Declaration by United Nations of January 1, 1942.

q: 23. Which one of the following is not an official language of the United Nations?
explain: The six official languages are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish. Portuguese is not an official language.

q: 24. Which of the following set of language is not UN General Assembly official language?
explain: Japanese is not an official UN language.

q: 25. How many countries were there in the existence of period of UNO?
explain: There were 51 founding members of the UN. Poland, although not represented at the San Francisco Conference, signed later and is considered an original member.

q: 26. The last country to sign the Charter of UNO was --------
explain: Poland was not at the San Francisco conference but left a space to sign as the 51st original member later.

q: 27. The Charter of UNO consists of ---------
explain: The UN Charter contains 19 chapters and 111 articles.

q: 28. How many articles are there in United Nation's Charter?
explain: The official UN Charter consists of 111 articles.

q: 29. The Headquarters of UNO, officially established in 1951 January 09, is located in-------
explain: The UN headquarters is located in New York City, on land purchased with a donation from John D. Rockefeller Jr.

q: 30. Which one of the following is/are an objective(s) of the UNO Charter?
options: To maintain international peace and security
explain: The preamble and Article 1 of the UN Charter encompass human rights, peace, security, and social/economic cooperation.

q: 31. The UN Charter is concerned with ---------
explain: The UN Charter is the binding constitutional document for all bodies and member states of the UN.

q: 32. Which country is the first to withdraw its membership of UNO?
explain: Indonesia was the first (and only) nation to attempt to withdraw from the UN in 1965, though it rejoined in 1966.

q: 33. Which of following given statement(s) is/are correct?
options: Currently, there 193 member nations in the United Nations organization
South Sudan is the 193th member of UNO
The last country to sign the Charter of UNO was Poland
explain: All the provided statements regarding member count, the 193rd member, and the 51st original signatory are factually correct.

q: 34. Which body of the United Nations Organizations is composed of all member states?
explain: The General Assembly is the only UN body in which all 193 member states have equal representation (one vote each).

q: 35. Which organ of the United Nations Organizations is responsible for coordinating the work its specialized agencies?
explain: ECOSOC (Economic and Social Council) coordinates the economic, social, and related work of the 15 UN specialized agencies.

q: 36. Who was the first woman president of United Nation General Assembly?
explain: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit of India was elected as the first woman president of the UN General Assembly in 1953.

q: 37. Which is the first country whose membership of UNO was dissolved?
explain: In 1971, the UN General Assembly recognized the People's Republic of China as the only legitimate representative of China to the UN, effectively expelling the representatives of Taiwan (Republic of China).

q: 38. Which one of the following is/are a function(s) of the UN General Assembly?
options: Any matter affecting International peace & Security
It passes UN budget of the UN.
It elects the Non- permanent members of the Security Council
explain: The General Assembly has the authority to discuss security, approve budgets, and elect non-permanent members of the Security Council.

q: 39. Which of the following is the main body of the United Nation organization?
explain: The General Assembly is considered the main deliberative, policymaking, and representative organ of the UN.

q: 40. Who is the person to deliver the longest speech in the General Assembly?
explain: Fidel Castro holds the record for the longest speech at the UN General Assembly, lasting 4 hours and 29 minutes in 1960.

q: 41. Which of the following organs of the United Nations Organization elects judges of the International court of Justice?
options: The Security Council and the General Assembly
The trusteeship council and the economic and social council
explain: Judges of the ICJ are elected simultaneously by the General Assembly and the Security Council.

q: 42. Which General Assembly was conducted as the millennium General Assembly by UNO?
explain: The 55th session of the UN General Assembly in 2000 was designated as the 'Millennium Assembly'.

q: 43. Which countries are the Permanent of the Security Council of UNO?
explain: The 'P5' are China, France, Russian Federation, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

q: 44. How many members of the United Nation's Security Council have veto power?
explain: Only the 5 permanent members of the Security Council possess the power to veto substantive resolutions.

q: 45. Which of the following is not permanent member of Security Council?
explain: Germany is not a permanent member; it frequently serves as an elected non-permanent member.

q: 46. In which year was Nepal first elected on a Non-Permanent member of the united Nation Security Council?
explain: Nepal served its first term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council during the 1969-1970 term.

q: 47. Nepal had been the temporary member of UN Security Council for ____ tenure.
explain: Nepal has served as a non-permanent (temporary) member of the Security Council twice: 1969-1970 and 1988-1989.

q: 48. The total number of members in Security Council of UN?
explain: The Security Council consists of 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.

q: 49. How many temporary members should be there in the provision of UNO Security Council?
explain: The UN Charter provides for 10 non-permanent (temporary) members, elected for two-year terms.

q: 50. Which one of the following is/are true regarding UN Security Council?
options: The first country to use veto power is Russia
The country to use veto for most number of times is Russia
The country to use least veto power is France
explain: Statistically, the USSR/Russia has used the veto most frequently, it was the first to use it, and France has used it the least among the major Western permanent members.

q: 51. Human Rights Council in the United Nations is the subsidiary organ of -----------
explain: The UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) was established in 2006 as a subsidiary body of the General Assembly, replacing the former Commission on Human Rights.

q: 52. Nepal had been the member of UN economic and Social Council for ____ tenure.
explain: Nepal has served four distinct terms as a member of ECOSOC, most recently for the 2024-2026 term.

q: 53. How many member counties are there in UNHCR?
explain: The Executive Committee of the High Commissioner's Programme (ExCom) governs UNHCR, and as per recent records in the text, it consists of 58 member countries (though this number has grown over time, we stick to the provided options).

q: 54. When was the International Court of Justice was established?
explain: The ICJ was established by the UN Charter in 1945 and began its operations in April 1946.

q: 55. The headquarters of International Court of Justice is located in ------
explain: The ICJ is the only principal organ of the UN not located in New York; it is seated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

q: 56. How many members are there in the International Court of Justice and what is their tenure?
explain: The Court is composed of 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.

q: 57. Which of the following nation has withdraw its membership from international court of criminal (ICC) in recent time?
explain: The Philippines officially withdrew from the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in March 2019.

q: 58. Who are the members of the General Assembly?
options: All members of the United Nations
All members of the Security Council
Permanent members of the Security Council
Members of the Economic and Social Council
explain: Every member state of the United Nations is represented in the General Assembly.

q: 59. Trusteeship Council suspended its operation since --------
explain: The Trusteeship Council suspended operations on November 1, 1994, after Palau, the last remaining UN trust territory, achieved independence.

q: 60. Why did the Trusteeship Council suspend its operation?
options: Due to the used of USA veto
due to completion of its mandate
due to disputes between Member States
explain: The Council's mission was to oversee the transition of trust territories to self-government or independence; it suspended operations because its mandate was fulfilled.

q: 61. Who was the first Secretary General of UNO?
explain: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving from 1946 to 1952.

q: 62. Which country does the ninth general of UNO Mr. Antonio Guterres belong?
explain: Antonio Guterres, who took office in 2017, is a Portuguese politician and diplomat.

q: 63. Antonio Guterres becomes the _____ Secretary General to visit Nepal.
explain: Following U Thant, Kurt Waldheim, Javier Pérez de Cuéllar, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, and Ban Ki-moon, Guterres became the 6th Secretary-General to visit Nepal.

q: 64. Who was the first Secretary General of UNO to Visit in Nepal?
explain: U Thant of Burma (Myanmar) was the first UN Secretary-General to visit Nepal in 1967.

q: 65. Who is the Secretary General of UNO died in plane Crash?
explain: Dag Hammarskjöld died in a plane crash in Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia) in 1961 while on a peace mission to the Congo.

q: 66. Which Secretary General of UN presented The Quiet Revolution Concept Paper?
explain: Kofi Annan presented 'The Quiet Revolution' as a series of reforms to renew the United Nations in 1997.

q: 67. Which organ of the United Nations cannot be attended by the Secretary General of the United Nations?
explain: While the SG serves as the chief administrative officer of most organs, the ICJ is an independent judicial body.

q: 68. For how many years is the Secretary General's working period at a time?
explain: The Secretary-General is appointed for a five-year term, which is renewable.

q: 69. Which Secretary General of United Nations, presented the report called Blue print agenda?
explain: Boutros Boutros-Ghali's 'An Agenda for Peace' (1992) is often referred to as a blueprint for UN preventive diplomacy and peacemaking.

q: 70. Secretary General of United Nations, whom was awarded with the Nobel Prize in Peace for the year 1961 A.D.?
explain: Dag Hammarskjöld was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize posthumously in 1961 for his efforts to strengthen the UN.

q: 71. Which of the following Specialized Agencies of United Nations awarded Noble peace prize for two times?
options: International Committees of the red cross
explain: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) won the prize in 1954 and 1981.

q: 72. Which of the following Organization awarded Noble peace prize for three times?
options: International committee of the Red Cross
explain: The ICRC was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1917, 1944, and 1963.

q: 73. When did international labor organization (ILO) received the Nobel Peace Prize?
explain: The ILO was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969 on the occasion of its 50th anniversary.

q: 74. When did international UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize?
explain: UNICEF was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965 for its efforts to promote brotherhood among nations.

q: 75. At which article of United Nations Charter, establishment of specialized agencies are mentioned?
explain: Article 57 of the UN Charter provides for the establishment of specialized agencies through intergovernmental agreements.

q: 76. What is the first specialized agency of UNO?
explain: The International Labour Organization (ILO), established in 1919, became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.

q: 77. Which UN Organization became the first to accept a donation in crypto currency?
explain: UNICEF launched its CryptoFund in 2019, becoming the first UN organization to hold and make transactions in cryptocurrency.

q: 78. Which of the following UN agencies focuses on poverty reduction and the improvement of living standards worldwide?
explain: The World Bank's primary goals are to end extreme poverty and promote shared prosperity globally.

q: 79. Which of the following is not organ of United Nations?
explain: The IMF is a specialized agency, not one of the six principal organs of the United Nations.

q: 80. Which of the following is a World Bank group of five institutions?
explain: The International Development Association (IDA) is one of the five institutions that make up the World Bank Group.

q: 81. The headquarters of International Atomic Energy Agency is located in -----------
explain: The IAEA, the world's 'Atoms for Peace and Development' organization, is headquartered in Vienna, Austria.

q: 82. WTO came into existence in the year ----------
explain: The World Trade Organization was established on January 1, 1995, following the Marrakesh Agreement.

q: 83. Which among the following is not a specialized agency of the United Nations Organization?
explain: While the WTO works closely with the UN, it is an independent organization and not a 'specialized agency' in the formal legal sense.

q: 84. Which one of the following is not the organ of United Nations?
explain: There is no 'Peace Keeping Coordination Council' among the six principal organs of the UN.

q: 85. Which of the following is not function of United Nations Development Program (UNDP)?
explain: The protection of refugees is the specific mandate of UNHCR, not UNDP.

q: 86. From which institution the concept of good governance has developed?
explain: The World Bank is credited with popularizing the concept of 'good governance' in the late 1980s as a condition for economic development.

q: 87. Which one of the following is not the organ of United Nations?
explain: Repeated question; 'Peace Keeping Coordination Council' is not a principal organ.

q: 88. Where is United Nations University located?
explain: The United Nations University (UNU) is headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan.

89. Match the Group I with Group II and choose the correct answer.
**Group I:** (a) ICAO (b) FAO (c) IMF (d) ILO
**Group II:** (1) Canada (2) Italy (3) USA (4) Switzerland
explain: ICAO is in Canada, FAO is in Italy, IMF is in USA, and ILO is in Switzerland.

q: 90. Which of the following UN agencies has its headquarters at Paris -----------
explain: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) is based in Paris, France.

q: 91. Which of the following is not an agency of UNO?
options: International Committee of the Red Cross
explain: The ICRC is an independent humanitarian institution and is not part of the UN system.

q: 92. The headquarters of Food and Agriculture Organization is in -----------
explain: The FAO is headquartered in Rome, Italy.

q: 93. The headquarters of World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is located in -----------
explain: WIPO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: 94. When ILO became a specialized agency of UN?
explain: While founded in 1919, the ILO became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.

q: 95. Which of the following UN agencies has received Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 A.D.?
explain: The World Food Programme (WFP) was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its efforts to combat hunger.

q: 96. Which of the following agencies assesses the "LDC Graduation"?
explain: LDC graduation is monitored by the Committee for Development Policy (CDP) under the UN Economic and Social Council.

q: 97. In which Country, UNO has spent highest quantity of Budget?
explain: Historically, in the context of these specific records, Haiti has seen significant UN spending due to humanitarian and peacekeeping efforts.

q: 98. The mission to which nation has been declared as the UN's most dangerous Peace keeping Mission --------
explain: MINUSMA in Mali is frequently cited as the deadliest/most dangerous UN peacekeeping mission.

q: 99. When was the Convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women issued?
explain: The CEDAW convention was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1979.

q: 100. As of August, 2024, there are ____ member states as the parties on UN convention against Corruption.
explain: As per the updated records provided, 191 states are parties to the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC).
